In hindsight, he should have noticed something. The signs were everywhere.

They were the last demigods in the dining table. The others having left earlier, this month's festivities making them busier than usual, especially Hysilens. Mydei should've been one of them, but unfortunately, his current predicament prevented him from performing his duties at an early hour.

"It's just… Lord Mydei, have you been sleeping well? I mean– I just noticed that you've been sleeping in lately and recently, I usually see you dozing off even during Lucid Hour."

His suspicions were right. He knows his recent behavior has been uncharacteristic of him. It was only a matter of time before someone questioned him.

"I– ," Mydei hesitates. "No, quite the contrary, I've been sleeping well lately. Too well even."

"Oh, I see. Maybe... it's because it's all over now? Maybe your body is finally getting all the rest it needs after everything you've been through," Castorice reasons with a small smile.

He frowns, not entirely convinced but having no other explanation otherwise. It would be strange to say so when the exhaustion only happened now, months after Era Nova — the actual Era Nova — was ushered in Amphoreus. And contrary to popular belief, he does rest. He, as a warrior, knows better than anyone how to take care of his body. The pair finished their meal in silence and left to go about their day.

Unfortunately for Mydei, the worst of the exhaustion lasted until the Month of Freedom, before subsiding completely by the Month of Reaping. Just in time for him to help with the month's harvest. The ones he's failed to mention to Phainon, knowing the alpha would be more insufferable with his hovering.

And, there's also the other thing. With the.. well… the milk leaking from his chest and the soreness that came with it. He doesn't think that it's normal even if Phainon says it's probably because he likes to suck on it so much.

With his plans for the day secured, Mydei eventually got ready for the day. While passing the Marmoreal Market on his way to Hyacine's clinic, he encountered said healer. She was carrying multiple boxes that towered over her in her arms, barely able to take a proper step with the boxes practically covering her face. Little Ica beside her somehow managing to hold onto a tinier box while also giving her tiny doots in direction.

He put away his teleslate where he had intended to contact Hyacine before he got distracted with a text sent by Phainon. The crown prince approached Hyacine just in time to steady her when she inevitably trip over a decoration she couldn't see.

"Lord Mydei! Oh my apologies. I didn't see you there." Little Ica also nuzzled him in greeting.

He chuckled, petting the chubby pegasus, "No doubt. Do you need help with that, Hyacine?"

"If it's no trouble with you then..."

"Don't worry about it. I was looking for you anyway." Mydei took several boxes from the healer's arms, carrying them as if it weighs nothing.

Hyacine's eyes widened in worry. "Looking for me? Did something happen? Are you injured? Sick?"

The prince shook his head in denial, quick to reassure the her. "No. It's nothing like that. It's just I've been feeling a lot… lethargic these past few weeks and I wanted to consult you for possible remedies."

"I see. I can examine you once we arrive at the clinic," Hyacine paused for a second before continuing, "Thinking about it, I do remember that Lord Phainon mentioned it to me earlier this week. He was so worried. I meant to check up on you but I forgot. My apologies."

Mydei sighed at her words. "You know how Phainon is. I wouldn't take it to heart…. probably. It might not even be as serious as he assumes it is. Anyway, we don't have to do it immediately. Since you seem busy with these." He nods to the boxes in both of their arms. "In fact, if you want, I can help you sort these out. I assume they are filled with supplies for the clinic."

"You may say so but I know how you sometimes underplay your own condition. Both you and Lord Phainon are very similar like that." Hyacine looked at Mydei with that unimpressed look of hers, while he averted his gaze, chagrined. "Lord Phainon is also someone who knows you better that anyone else. If he's worried, then I'm sure there's a reason for that."

"Doot. Doot."

"See. Even Little Ica agrees!"

Mydei just smiled, saying nothing in reply and continued walking towards the location of Hyacine's clinic.

Hyacine continued, "And if you still want to help, then we can arrange these after I examine you. My assistants are all busy with minor check-ups, as well as preparing for the first-aid booths around Okhema so your help is much appreciated."

"Alright, you win, Hyacine." Mydei sighed, having nothing to rebuke the Sky Demigod's words. Meanwhile, it seemed that in the span of their conversation, they had already reached the clinic. The lobby was filled with patients, though luckily none of them seem to be bad enough to need Hyacine's input. She led Mydei to the back of the clinic, entering through the back door that leads to her personal office.

“That's right, Lord Mydei, where's Lord Phainon? Usually, the both of you are always together, but you're alone this time. And I would've expected him to cling to you with how worried he had been." Hyacine then gestured to an empty spot in the clinic. "Please just place the boxes over there.”

“He's out helping the citizens set up some last minute decorations for the festival. Aglaea's orders. He also mentioned greeting the Astral Express since they'll be arriving in a few quints.” Mydei placed the boxes down the spot Hyacine pointed out, recalling the text message Phainon sent.

"I see. Now why don't you sit down first. Let me get a few things first." Mydei heeded her words and sat down on the chair in front of her office desk. He didn't have to wait long before Hyacine took her place behind the desk. She placed what seemed to be a medical records. His medical records to be exact. It was a lot thicker than he thought it to be considering he doesn't usually get sick. But thinking about it, it could also be filled with the injuries that Hyacine insisted he get treated for even if he's immortal.

"First things first. Why don't you explain to me what you've been feeling these past few weeks. Actually why not start since the first time you've felt the exhaustion. Lord Phainon mentioned that it had already happened before but it faded? Please tell everything you've been feeling since then, any symptoms you can think of."

Mydei nodded. "That's right. It started around eight? months ago. Or maybe nine. It just happened for no reason at all. It lasted until the Month of Reaping but after that I feel energized. And then it came back around the last two months."

"Hmmm. Anything else happened between those months?"

"There was also the cravings. At first, I only felt strong urges for normal food but then it escalated until Phainon had to stop me from eating feeds for dromas." Mydei wasn't sure if he should also add this but… "I've also been feeling weird mood swings back then. Only my upbringing stopped me from crying during those times." He felt embarrassed admitting to that.

Suspicion arose in Hyacine's features. She gestured him to continue.

"There was also the high… libido. I almost felt insatiable." By now Mydei's cheeks were flushed in complete embarrassed but he had a feeling it was important for Hyacine to know about this. "My chest too. It's really sore nowadays. And m-milk was leaking from it. Ahem. Phainon says it's because he likes to suck on it but I'm not really sure."

Hyacine grateful for the honestly but she really did not need to hear about the last part, actually.

Just then, a sharp cramp in his stomach interrupted his words, but he continued on as if it was nothing. Just subtly placing his hand on his stomach. If someone else was looking, they probably wouldn't have noticed something was wrong, but not Hyacine.

"Lord Mydei. I think this isn't just about the exhaustion, isn't it?" Hyacine frowned at him, always so perceptive. "Since we met earlier, you’ve been feeling some kind of pain, right? You even almost stumbled on the way here and now, I see you clutching your stomach as if in pain. Lord Mydei, please don't hide anything from me anymore. Please let me help you."

"My apologies, Hyacine." Mydei couldn't help the twinge of guilt he felt at the other's earnest words. "I didn't mean to hide it. It's just that… I kind of forgot to mention it? I mean, I meant to hide it from Phainon but I suppose that just made me hide it from you, unconsciously."

Hyacine made a face at the word forgot, but Mydei hardly blame her. He really did mean to mention it since it was the one thing he also needs to remedy before Phainon finds out. He continued on, "This one started just a few days ago. Back then, it was only mild and it happens irregularly. I almost couldn't feel it. It was like my stomach was cramping, like when I get hungry, but different? I guess. Then just now, it's happening more frequently."

The suspicion in Hyacine's features only grew. “Lord Mydei, can you get on the examination bed in the other room? I have a feeling I know what this is about, but… it shouldn't be possible." She shook her head. "No. Nevermind that. I'll just have to confirm it then."

Mydei made to move towards the other room, but the strange cramps hit him again just as he entered the space, making him stumble. Hyacine and Little Ica was quick to support and help him get on the bed. Once he was settled, the healer looks up at him for permission. He simply nods his assent and watches as she examined his stomach. Her face paling at what she discovered.

Hyacine asks him with a faint voice, "Lord Mydei. The cramps before, how long were the intervals before the next one?"

"Around two minutes," Mydei answers with growing concern. Hyacine's uttered profanities at his answer didn't help his case. "Hyacine, what's wrong? Am i actually poisoned? Am i dying?"

The Sky Demigod quickly composed herself. "N–no. It's not that. It's just– Lord Mydei, you're currently in labor."

The other's words made Mydei speechless. He honestly couldn't believe her words. He would have thought she was joking if weren't for the fact that he knows she is never the type to do that. Or maybe she's trying something new. Or it could be that it was Cipher impersonating Hyacine right now. Maybe.

"Labor? You mean like, working?" Yeah that has to be it. She must've meant something else. Nevermind how the meaning wouldn't make sense with the wording.

"No. As in childbirth. As in there's currently a baby inside of you that's trying to get out."

"But that's not–"

"I know it's not possible! But it's the truth and there's no time now. You're already on active labor. Please stay here while I prepare some things." It's a testament to how rattled Hyacine is if the normally respectful woman is interrupting him like this.

Mydei watches her run out of the room, still in a daze at how the situation has escalated. Little Ica offering little doots of comfort beside him. He placed a hand on his stomach. A baby. His and Phainon's baby. Because there's no one else who could be the baby's father. For the longest time, he had already accepted that this would be the one thing he would never have. But now, to think it was actually possible. However, the moment was broken when a sharp cramp– no a contraction hit him. Along with it was a burst of fluid that came out from below him. It made everything even more real.

"I know. I know. Please just wait a little longer, little one. Hyacine will be back soon. You probably can't wait to meet us, huh?" Mydei caressed his stomach, waiting for the contraction to end.

Hyacine came back inside the room soon enough, bringing a wheelchair and an assistant with her. Seeing his drenched pants, she took a medical robe from one of the cabinets and handed it to him. He was quick to change and then both healer and assistant helped him get on the wheelchair before he's being wheeled into another room. This one seemed to be intended for delivery. He was then helped into the medical bed lying in the middle of the room.

Hyacine moved to leave Mydei's side but a hand on her sleeve held her back. She looked at him in confusion. "Phainon–" Mydei called out but another contraction interrupted him. Hyacine understood immediately and comforted the other.

"Don't worry, Lord Mydei. I already contacted Lady Aglaea to inform Lord Phainon about this." At this, Mydei let go of her sleeve and allowed himself to fall back on the bed. Hyacine busied herself with the tools. Little Ica as well was darting around the room, as if checking if everything is in order.

Just then, a head of pink hair burst through the door. Cyrene.

"Little prince!" She rushed to Mydei, gripping his hand in comfort. "Don't worry, Phainon's on his way. I have some experience with this so I'll be here to help." She stayed there letting him clutch her hand in pain, even though his grip must have gotten painful. She stayed there for a few more contractions until Phainon arrived and took her place.

"Mydei–" Phainon cried out, completely out of breath and sweaty.

"Y-you're late, Deliverer. Haha. You look absolutely disheveled." Mydei laughed at his partner. Still managing to feel amusement despite the pain he's in.

"Of course. I shouldn't have left you. I knew something was wrong and yet…"

"Do not act like I'm dying, Deliverer. I'm not. In fact, I am giving new life. Our child. They'll be here soon. I only lament that I didn't find out sooner."

"Lord Phainon, can you move aside for a bit?" Hyacine interrupted them. "I need to check on Lord Mydei, may I? I have to see how far along you are."

Hyacine checked on him but unfortunately, he's still not ready to push. She told them to sit tight because it might take a while before it happens.

To be honest, Mydei thought he knew pain. But this was a different pain altogether.

That was all he could feel. The pain.

He doesn't usually feel pain this bad, having since long been desensitized to pain with his countless deaths.

"Breathe, Mydei. Just breathe and relax. It'll be over soon." And there's a mosquito yapping at his ears. He tried to appreciate it really. His sweet mate trying to make things better for him. But–

His hand shot up at Phainon's sprout. "Say breathe one more fucking time and I'll fucking gut you right where you stand."

Phainon thankfully shut up and surrendered to his role of being Mydei's stress ball — albeit a hand shaped one that gives off little crunchy sounds when gripped too hard.

Three quints later and Mydei is slowly losing his mind. Who would've thought that what the Sea of Souls have failed to do, childbirth succeeded on. He's pretty sure he had already crushed Phainon's hand to pieces. Or maybe to dust. He'll apologize later but right now he honestly doesn't have the mind to care. Fortunately for him (and Phainon's hand), Hyacine had deemed him ready and told him to push.

"Lord Mydei, just push with all your might when you feel the urge." Hyacine instructed from infront of his spread legs, her hands poised to catch the baby. Mydei did just that and screamed in pain at the effort it took.

"Keep going. I can see their head already."

It took a while but finally, a tiny body was being held carefully in Hyacine's arms. Tiny cries coming from frail lungs. And oh–

This must have been what mother felt.

"It's a healthy baby girl, Lord Mydei, Lord Phainon," Hyacine said with a smile, handing the baby over to Cyrene for the clean-up after cutting off the umbilical cord. She then focused her attention back to Mydei. "You may feel some more contractions, but those are for the placenta and are usually mild."

That was what she said, however the next contraction feel the same as before. Mydei bent over in pain. "Hyacine! Something's wrong–"

Hyacine was quick to examine him again. But what she found made her freeze before snapping put of it. "My apologies, Lord Mydei! There's another one. The process is similar to the first baby so please just do it as before."

Pause.

Wait.

What.

"A-another one? Twins?!" Phainon asked with his jaw dropped. Already in a state of astonishment because of the miracle that is their first baby, but there's actually another one?

"Ready, Lord Mydei?" Hyacine ignored Phainon, focusing only on her patient. Mydei nodded. Steadying himself for another push.

This one took longer, about half a quint, but luckily they were graced with another tiny body emitting tiny cries. After Cyrene took this one away too, Hyacine quickly checked if there's another one or if this is the last of it. Fortunately, there's none so she can get back to dealing with the afterbirth.

On Mydei's side, he was still in a daze, still taking time to come back to the real world. Childbirth is a war in and of itself, Mydei thought to himself, saluting every woman and omega in the world. They should be awarded the same when soldiers come home from war. He snapped out of it when he heard the cries.

He looked over to see Cyrene had handed one baby off to Phainon and was about to hand over the other to him. He quickly took the baby in his arms, his previous experience in handling newborns coming in handy.

"Congratulations, Dei, Phainon. It's a healthy baby girl and a healthy baby boy. The older one is with Mydei, the younger with Phainon." Cyrene smiled at the new parents, tears brimming from her eyes.

Phainon adjusted his position, letting Mydei look at their son in his arms. What Mydei saw made him laugh. His voice incredibly fond. "Nine months in my belly and they both look like their stupid dad."

As if sensing their mother's amusement, the twins opened their eyes. The both of them have light blue eyes, though if what Mydei has learned before was right, it might change in the next few months. Maybe there's still a chance they have his eyes.

He only knows them for a short while, but he is already ready to do anything for, even brave the Sea of Souls once again. And looking at his mate beside him, he knows Phainon will do the same.

Cyrene and Hyacine let the couple have their moment for a few more minutes before addressing the main question with this situation. Just how exactly did an alpha like Mydei give birth. And they both already have an inkling as to why.

"Phainon? Can you come here for a sec?" Hyacine called out to her former classmate. Phainon seemed a bit unwilling to leave Mydei's side but ultimately gave the now sleeping twin he was holding to Cyrene who took the other one and placed them on the bassinet near the bed.

Hyacine examined him and also took his blood. She ran off with her notes and vial of blood in her hands and Ica on her heels. Phainon watched her go with a confused look in his face. Cyrene beckoned to him, gesturing him to take a seat. With both of her audience's attention on her, she began narrating a story.

"Did you know? In the legends of past heroes, there was a case such as yours, Phainon. There was a princess of noble blood that everyone believed to be an alpha. She was a follower of Kephale and a powerful warrior of her own right. Everyone believed her to settle with an omega of her standing, but she chose another alpha instead. A male alpha commoner soldier. It spark thousands of controversy. Many lamented that such a powerful alpha was to be reduced to nothing but a bearer for the soldier's children.

"However, one day, her lover fainted, pain wrecked his body, and from it, a baby was born. One that looked so much like her, no one could deny the baby's parentage. Many believed the soldier to be hiding his real presentation, but that was soon debunked. Then, they assumed it was a curse from the black tide, but no such signs were found. Lastly, healers examined both alphas and the truth was laid bare. There were no anomalies found on the commoner alpha's body, but they could see differences in the princess when compared to a normal alpha. People called this noble princess an enigma.

"But everyone believed it to be just myths. When I asked Lady Cerydra and Lady Hysilens about it, they also assumed an enigma's existence to be mere stuff of legends since they've never met one before. Until you, that is." Cyrene finished her story. Both Mydei and Phainon were quiet in the conclusion she made.

"So Phainon's an enigma? I've never heard of that term before." It was only natural. Since childhood until just recently, Mydei's life has only revolved around war and battle tactics. Only in the past few months was he able to venture to other aspects of life.

"Well, that's the only explanation I can think of," Cyrene replied. "And these days, all people talk about were stories of us. Legends of the past are rarely being talked about now."

Phainon laughed, rubbing his hand behind his head. "I honestly thought enigmas could only be found in Castorice's stories. I didn't know it was an actual thing." The other two sighed at his words, not surprised. They know how Castorice likes to include actual historical facts in her stories even in the most amorous ones. But apparently Phainon didn't realize this yet.

"They’re real and one of them is currently in this room." It was Hyacine. It seems she was back from whatever she was looking for. "Sorry it took so long. I had find records of the previous case, and there were multiple false records in the files. I had to sort them out. But, I can confirm it. Lord Phainon is indeed an enigma."

"Case closed, it seems." Cyrene smiled at them. "Anyway, do you guys have any ideas for names?"

At that, both Phainon and Mydei turned to look at each other. Then Phainon broke eye contact to look at her.

"I have some ideas," he confessed quietly. At the other three's stunned faces, he immediately backtracked, falling over himself trying to explain. "I mean– it's just– I was just… thinking. About what Cyrene said a few months ago in the Garden of Life. I couldn't get it out of my head no matter how impossible it seemed back then. And now, well…"

Mydei understood. After all, he, too, couldn't stop thinking about it, but he certainly did not go as far as to think of names. It came handy now though, he admits. Who would've thought Cyrene's prediction would actually come true. "Well? Let's hear it then."

"I was thinking for boys, it would be Perseus or Sirius. As for girls," Phainon paused before continuing. "I was thinking of Calliope or Penelope. Other names were Callisto or Astraea or Pheobe, but of course if you don't like them, I can think of others or maybe you can pick them–"

Mydei pulled him into a kiss, interrupting his ramblings. Phainon melted into him. The two women in the room carefully looked away, busying themselves with this or that. "Let's go with that then."

"Uhh. Which one?"

Mydei rolled his eyes. "Calliope and Perseus. It seems fitting."

"Okay. Anything you want." Tears started falling from Phainon's eyes and Mydei only looked at him with so much love. It was all quiet for a while before Mydei remembered something.

"Wait! The festival!"

"Oh, don't worry about that, Dei. Aglaea and the others have already dealt with it. It's fine if a few demigods don't show themselves. It's best if you focus on yourself right now." Cyrene was quick to assure him. "Besides there are still a lot of things to take care of, especially since you weren't prepared for their arrival. For example, the clothes for the babies, preparing the nursery, how to take care of newborns. Things like that."

"I can give you some pamphlets and brochures for now, but I am expecting you to attend a few classes the Twilight Courtyard are hosting," Hyacine added.

They were truly lucky to have them as friends. Phainon can feel tears gathering at his eyes again. The day had developed into one he never expected to happen. Blessings and miracles have come to his and Mydei's way. And two new precious members of their family arrived in their life.

"Anyway, we should transfer you into a more comfortable room to rest." Hyacine stood up from the seat she took a while ago without them noticing. She added apologetically, "I know you might want to rest in the comfort of your own home, but I can't let you leave until I completely cleared all of you. I also need to settle the documents for the little ones."

"I understand Hyacine," Mydei said with smile.

Later in the new room, it was just the two them and their two little ones left. Cyrene had left a while ago with the offer of turning the spare bedroom they have in their house into a nursery. The big smile she has on her face suggests that she will have fun designing the nursery. Fortunately unlike Phainon, Cyrene actually have good eyes for design so Mydei can trust her judgment.

By the window of the room was Phainon, Calliope in his arms. She had woken up a while ago so Phainon is currently trying to lull her to sleep. He is singing a lullaby that Mydei had heard him sing to kids they were babysitting before. He had mentioned it was a lullaby his parents used to sing to him. Now, he was singing it to their daughter.

"You really do make a good dad." Mydei said almost quietly. He was currently cradling a still sleeping Perseus. Mydei won't admit it but he, like Phainon, had dreams like this before. Dreams he thought would never come true.

Phainon stopped his singing, Calliope already falling asleep. He turned his gaze outside. "Did you know, everytime I see you with the children of Amphoreus, I always felt guilty that I couldn't give you this."

"I know. You told me that before. But you did, didn't you? Gave me this. Two healthy children." Then with a teasing voice. "And maybe more on the way? After all, didn't you promise me a child who looks like me?"

"Mydei! Not in front of the kids," Phainon hissed, finally looking back at Mydei. "Well, I wouldn't mind. I do want to take care of you when you're pregnant. And we can take care of all of them no matter how many. We have the means and we're also not short on friends and family helping us. Plus, Amphoreus is peaceful right now."

"Then… let's have more kids, hmmm? Papa." Mydei can see how Phainon likes being called that no matter how much he might try to deny it. His cute lover should get used to it, he thinks as he laughs at the other's groan.

It was already Curtain-Fall Hour but the city outside was still very lively. Flashes of light bursting though the windows. It was only Hyacine's rainbow shield that muffled the sounds and dimmed the lights for the patients of Twilight Courtyard. It was also because of the festivities outside that the healer suggested they leave in the morning when it's more quiet.

“You know, Mydei, I should've known something was wrong when you didn't scold me for calling you princess back then,” Phainon said with a laugh. The both of them standing near the doorway of the spare bedroom-turned‐nursery. Cyrene did a great job with it. They had just managed to place the twins in the cribs she prepared for them.

“HKS. Why are you still calling me that? You already have a princess and a prince as well right in front of you,” Mydei gestured to Calliope and Perseus sleeping peacefully in their crib.

“You're right. You're right. The mother of a princess and a prince is a queen, right? How about that, my queen?”

Mydei could only drag his lover away from the nursery to beat him senseless far from where they could disturb their sleeping children.

This actually ended up completely different from my initial plans, like this was supposed to be only 1-2k words, and Phainon was also not meant to be present during birth, but he wrote himself in. He wants to support his wife, I guess.
